chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had intercourse with his wife during the month of Ramadan and could not find what to give in charity to sixty poor people, he said: He gives in charity according to his ability. And it has been narrated that it is permissible for him to fast eighteen days in place of two months.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife in Ramadan if he cannot feed sixty poor people?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar highlights the juristic flexibility in expiation (kaffarah) for breaking the fast in Ramadan, specifically addressing the inability to feed sixty poor people. It records the view that one may substitute the standard sixty days of fasting with eighteen days, reflecting the Shia tradition of varying opinions on the duration of fasting as a substitute for feeding the needy. This underscores the principle of ease (yusr) in Islamic law when financial means are limited.
